safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold specifies E45 cream and antihistamines with minimal relief; generated only states 'failed OTC creams' without mentioning antihistamines or E45.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting that the patient already tried E45 and antihistamines with minimal relief reduces the usefulness of the history for gauging what has or hasn’t worked and may lead to redundant or less targeted recommendations, but it is unlikely to directly cause immediate clinical harm. The key diagnosis and overall management plan (avoid irritants/gloves, emollients, topical steroid) would typically remain similar.

safety_verdicts.content: Prescribed a steroid cream to be used twice daily (BD).
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold specifies steroid cream twice daily (BD); generated mentions topical steroid cream but does not include BD/twice daily frequency.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not documenting the intended topical steroid frequency (BD/twice daily) creates a medication-instruction gap that can plausibly lead to under-treatment (persistent pain/cracking, delayed recovery) or overuse (skin atrophy/irritation), particularly if the note is used to generate or reconcile instructions. Dosing/frequency errors are higher-risk than general narrative omissions because they can directly change medication exposure.
